findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A soiled pair of scissors is observed in storage alongside spoons ready for customer service. Discussion revealed that it is used for cutting the milks bags in the Prairie Farms dispenser. This means that the observed soilage is residual milk and should not be in contact with the spoons. A server removed the scissors to correct. Ensure that all cleaned food contact surfaces are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

1) A long drip is observed on the hood system over the fryers. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The drip was removed to correct. 2) Food debris (and possible mold) is observed on the wire shelving in the standing cooler across from the steam table. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean to prevent possible contamination of the foods beneath. Ensure that all locations are maintained clean when they are in proximity to containers of food. 3) (REPEAT) Wire shelving in the standing cooler across from the steam table in the kitchen is chipping/rusting. This poses a concern for physical contaminations in the foods beneath. The PIC is instructed to reseal and/or replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC during the majority of this inspection does not currently have a completed allergen training certificate. The situation was discussed and they are instructed to complete a course and maintain a certificate moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing with all employees. Ensure that all employees wash hands at all times that it is required.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple dented cans are observed on the rack in the storage area. The PIC was shown and discarded the cans during this inspection to correct. Ensure all dented cans are separated for credit/discard in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

Two of the four sani buckets in the facility are observed to not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets to correct. The front of house bucket observed in this way was recently changed per employees. Education took place. Change sani rags when the buckets are changed to not dilute the new solution with the old that is still stored in the rag. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels of concentration at all times in the facility.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. 

A phone is observed on the counter next to food preparation in the back of the facility. The PIC was consulted and the phone removed to correct. Ensure that personal items are stored away from food preparation surfaces.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Multiple pans and lids are observed in storage that do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to storage. The noted items were discussed with the PIC and the items moved to dish for re-cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are thoroughly cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

The steam well at the prep line is observed to be holding cheese sauce and gravy at 128F-130F. It appears that the equipment kicked off. Items were brought out approximately one hour prior to observation. The equipment was reset and the foods allowed to be reheated on the stove to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple locations throughout the facility are in need of cleaning. Areas include: 1) the fan covers in the walk in cooler; 2) shelves in the walk in cooler; 3) wall/ floor junctions in the dry storage area and next to the soda syrup equipment; 4) the can rack in the dry storage area; 5) on top of the center stove in the kitchen; 6) under the oven in the kitchen; 7) on the side of the fryer next to the stove; 8) the fan cover aimed towards the dish area and; 9) the fan cover in the standing cooler next to the door into the dry storage area. Ensure that all areas of the facility are maintained clean.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The prep cooler to the right of the grill area is not effectively holding temperature. Follow up would normally be 2 weeks, but inspector will be on vacation. Follow up is set for 6/12/23 for repair/compliance.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The prep cooler to the right of the grill is holding foods between 52F-56F internal temperatures. Per the PIC, items in this cooler were stocked at 7 am (just under 2 hours). Items were allowed to be placed into another cooler for rapid cooling. Ice baths were discussed moving foreword and Inspector will follow up in the future (refer to line item #1).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Sani buckets throughout the facility are observed low during this inspection. Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct the violation. This is the second inspection in a row where buckets were observed low however, so the violation is a repeat at this time.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. 

1) Multiple items in the steam table along the main kitchen walkway are observed between 112F and 120F. Items were prepared fresh this morning at approximately 7 am. The steam table has been turned up and the TCS items will be discarded at 11 am (4 hours). Items include cheese sauce, gravy and sausage. 2) Chili is observed with an internal temperature of 123 in the steam table to the right of the fryer. Foods in the other lines are observed at correct temperatures. Investigation indicated that the water was nearly out in the bottom of the line and is believed to be why the equipment was not functioning correctly in this spot only. Water was added to correct the situation and the chili is observed at correct temperatures at the end of the inspection. Chili will still need to be discarded by 11 am (4 hours) due to temperature abuse.

findings.comment:
Observed employee crack raw shell eggs onto the grill with gloved hands, cook the eggs, plate them with a spatula, then plate toast with their gloved hands without any handwashing. Employees must wash hands when moving from raw foods (shell eggs) to ready-to-eat foods (toast). CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC and provided education.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

CORRECTED— Discussed using 4-hour Time as a Control for foods in the prep cooler while air conditioning issues persist (expected to be resolved tomorrow). findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12. Dishwasher not washing between clean and dirty dishes.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on cream cheese in walk-in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer?s use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11  (Pf) A consumer advisory is not provided for serving raw or undercooked food. Discussed disclosure and reminder requirements. Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions. Reference 3-603.11. Provided consumer advisory.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored

Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on floors, walls, and ceiling. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Shake machine, mixer, and cooler.

findings.title: Allergen training as required

findings.comment:

750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed an ice scoop being stored with the handle in the ice. Ice scoop moved during the inspection. 
750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed old, inoperable refrigerator, being used for storage of equipment, to have a soiled base and inside the cooling area. Clean this area.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the prep back kitchen to have soiled walls and ceilings. Ensure that this area is cleaned. 2) The nudo board throughout the kitchen should be repaired so that it is smooth with the wall. (Kitchen area by Omelete prep). 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed several items in the reach in cooler that were either not dated or were past the 7 days allowed for ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods. These items included tomato sauce dated 8/2, baked beans dated 8/6, coleslaw dated 8/7 and noodles and sloppy joes with no date. These items were discarded during the inspection with the exception of the noodles, which were reported to have been made 2 days ago and were dated at such. Make sure to mark each ready to eat, potentially hazardous food with the date of preparation or opening and hold no longer than 7 days maximum (Monday - Sunday, etc as discussed).
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed an employee beverage sitting on the prep table next to the prep cooler. Store personal beverages in areas away from and below food and dishes used for the public. Ideally store personal beverages near hand sinks so that you can wash your hands after touching your beverage.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed both ice bins up front to be stored in the open position when not in use. Pull lids to ice bins closed when not in use.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed coving to be missing or in disrepair along the back wall behind the prep table. Repair or replace or provide coving throughout the facility so there is not a gap between the wall and floor.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the caulking near the hand sink to be cracked. 2) Observed there to be a gap between the nudo board and the trim along the door along the back prep area wall leading into the kitchen. Make sure all walls and caulk are smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed soiled tools being stored above food for service in the dry storage area of the facility. Ensure that items used for the maintenance of the facility are stored separately from the food and food contact surfaces of the facility. Tools were moved during the inspection. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee preparing food with gloves on, remove their gloves, and begin handling RTE food. Ensure that RTE food is handled with gloves on. Hands should also be washed prior to donning a new set of gloves. Employee was educated and instructed to rewash their hands. 
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service articles being stored on top of a cooler on the prep line with the food contact surface up and no cover provided. Ensure that single service articles are either stored inverted on a clean surface or under a cover to prevent contamination of the food contact surface. Single service were moved during the inspection. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 1 live roach and 3 dead roaches in the dish area of the facility. Manager states they use Sentinel for pest control and will request an additional visit. Ensure that proper cleaning and maintenance is being done on the facility to prevent future pest issues. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed coving throughout the facility to be missing or in disrepair. The coving should repaired or replaced to not allow a gap between the wall and the floors. This could assist in mitigating pest issues in the facility. 
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed caulking throughout the facility to be in disrepair. Owner states he is working towards replacing the caulking in these areas. 2) The nudo board is also pulling away from the wall on the prep line. Ensure that this board is resecured to the wall. 3) The walls and coving throughout the kitchen and dish area were noted to be soiled. Cleaning should be done throughout the facility on the walls and coving. This could assist in mitigating pest issues in the future. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily cleanable and shall be maintained in good repair.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed cheeseburger soup, within the walk-in freezer, that was probed from 80F on the outer edge to 140F at the center. The product did not have a time mark and was believed to have been placed in the freezer between 8 and 8:30 AM. The product was also sitting in a deeper, plastic container with the lid on it. Ensure that when cooling products, they are placed in shallow containers to increase surface area exposed to the cool air. Utilization of the ice paddle would also help the product cool quicker. Soup was reheated to 165F and cooling process started over again. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed chili in a steam well to be probed at 125-130F. The chili was placed in the steam well at 8AM, after being brought to a boil. The steam table temperature was turned up and the product was labeled for discard at 1PM. Ensure that if items are going to be hot held, then they are held above 135F. Monitoring of these temperatures will help recognize issues in the future. 
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop for the ice machine sitting in a container with standing water and food debris. The container does not have a drain and is not removable from the wall for easy cleaning. Ensure that this container is maintained in a clean state so as to prevent potentials for cross contamination into the ice. Ice scoop moved to different location, after being ran through dish machine. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed an ice scoop being stored, with the handle in the ice, at the front service counter. Ensure that ice scoops are stored in the proper manners listed below. Ice scoop moved during the inspection. 
750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice machine to have the lid becoming in disrepair. The back of the lid has started to pull away, which is allowing the insulation to be exposred to the ice. Ensure that the lid is replaced or repaired to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the plumbing below the dish machine to be in disrepair allowing excessive water to accumulate in this area. This is leading to standing water in grooves in the floor, as well as in holes where plumbing comes through the wall. This could eventually lead to rot within the wall and pest issues within the facility. Ensure that the plumbing is repaired so that it drains properly. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed an area of the floor by the dish machine to not have any tiling or coving. This is causing an area that is lower than the rest of the floor, which is leading to water accumulation in the area (see violation 29). Ensure that the floor is maintained in good repair, that is smooth, easily cleanable, and in a clean state. 
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed a hole in the wall, where plumbing comes through the wall, by the dish machine. This hole is allowing excessive water accumulations to leak back into the wall. This could lead to further pest and structural problems within the facility. 2) Observed the caulking at the hand sink to have mold accumulations and be in disrepair. Ensure that the caulking is cleaned or replaced. Due to the state of the caulking, it is recommended that it be stripped and replaced. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily cleanable and shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: Observed a spray bottle of chemicals that was unlabeled. The owner stated it was "Pot & Pan Cleaner" and that he had made it the night before. Ensure that all chemical containers are properly labeled to reduce the chances of cross contamination. The owner was allowed to label the bottle during the inspection. 750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
